hints: Focus on what points 1, 2, 3 and 4 mean. Remember valves open and close when pressure on one side becomes higher than on the other side, so look for where the left ventricle line crosses the left atrium line and the aorta line.

Both sets of valves are closed twice per cycle, once between 1 and 2 during ventricular contraction and once between 3 and 4 during ventricular relaxation. Read the time difference for each small gap off the x-axis and add them together.
walkthrough:
**Recall when valves open and close**

Think pressure differences, not time. The AV valve closes when ventricle pressure rises above atrium pressure. The semilunar valve opens when ventricle pressure rises above aorta pressure.

So point 1 = AV closes, point 2 = semilunar opens, point 3 = semilunar closes, point 4 = AV opens.

**Find the first both-closed period, 1 to 2**

Between 1 and 2 the AV is already closed but the semilunar is not yet open, so both are closed. This is isovolumetric contraction.

From the graph: point 1 is at about $0.12 \text{ s}$, point 2 is at about $0.15 \text{ s}$.
$$0.15 - 0.12 = 0.03 \text{ s}$$

**Find the second both-closed period, 3 to 4**

Between 3 and 4 the semilunar has already closed but the AV has not yet opened, so both are closed again. This is isovolumetric relaxation.

From the graph: point 3 is at about $0.36 \text{ s}$, point 4 is at about $0.40 \text{ s}$.
$$0.40 - 0.36 = 0.04 \text{ s}$$

**Add the two periods for the total**

The question asks for the total time in one $0.6 \text{ s}$ cycle when both are closed.
$$0.03 + 0.04 = 0.07 \text{ s}$$

options.A: 0.03 s is only the first gap from 1 to 2 when both valves are closed during contraction. It misses the second gap from 3 to 4.
options.B: 0.04 s is only the second gap from 3 to 4 when both valves are closed during relaxation. It misses the first gap from 1 to 2.
options.C: 0.07 s is correct because it adds both isovolumetric periods: about 0.03 s (1 to 2) plus about 0.04 s (3 to 4).
options.D: 0.21 s is the ventricular ejection period from 2 to 3 when the semilunar valve is open, not the time when both valves are closed.
